findings.title: Module-level names removed from mark_failed without compatibility aliases
findings.body: Before this change, `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` exposed `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`, and the `SimpleCheckIn` TypedDict. All of these are now removed from that module (moved to the new `incidents`/`incident_occurrence` modules and `monitors.types`, and renamed, e.g. `mark_failed_threshold` -> `try_incident_threshold`) with no import aliases left behind. Any existing consumer — including test modules such as `tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py` — that imports these names from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` will now fail with an ImportError. The PR contains no test or caller updates (only 4 files changed), so this either breaks those consumers or leaves them silently stale. The refactor should either keep re-export aliases in `mark_failed.py` or update all importers in the same PR.

findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context computes a humanized config copy but returns the original config
findings.body: In `get_monitor_environment_context`, lines 160-162 build a modified copy of the monitor config (`config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` and replace `schedule_type` with its human-readable display value), but the returned dict's `"config"` key uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` directly instead of the local `config` variable. As a result the `schedule_type` display value is never included in the monitor context attached to the incident occurrence, and the copied/modified variable is dead code. The return should use the local `config` (e.g. `"config": config`). This was carried over verbatim from the old `mark_failed.py`, but since this PR creates the new canonical home for this logic, the dead code should be fixed here.
